# Train a custom protein model

## Prepare the data

Use a table with one sequence per row and a clearly named target column. For classification, keep class definitions and label encoding consistent. For regression, specify the measurement and units. Remove duplicate leakage across splits and keep related proteins in the same group when needed.

```csv
sequence,label
MKTAYIAKQRQISFVKSHFSRQ,0
GAVLILKKKGHHEAELKPLAQ,1
```

This example shows a file format, not enough data to train a useful model. Keep a separate final test set; do not use its labels for model selection.

## Submit training

1. Open the custom model Training entry in Model Plaza.
2. Upload data and select the sequence/label columns or dataset fields shown by the form.
3. Choose the backbone and training method. Review epochs, batch size, learning rate and any method-specific settings.
4. Submit the job. Training is queued along with other compute work; follow its job status and logs instead of submitting again.
5. Open the resulting checkpoint, configuration and metrics, then [evaluate](./Evaluation.md) and [predict](./Prediction.md).

## Online and local

Online custom training only supports **ESM2-8M**, with server-enforced budgets and uploads up to **10 MB per file**. Larger backbones remain unavailable online. This bounded web training form is distinct from unrestricted PLM training tools, which are local-only.

Local deployments can offer additional configured backbones and methods, subject to installed weights, dependencies, hardware and administrator switches. The platform imposes no local upload-size cap, but disk and runtime resources still apply.

## Algorithm research and delivery

Use Scientist for custom algorithms or iterative experiments rather than assuming every model must fine-tune a PLM. Lightweight methods can run in the session sandbox. Ask for evaluation, baselines, source code, an input/output example and artifact files.

For Agent tool-based training locally, the caller supplies explicit parameters to the configuration tool. The tool returns the resolved settings without asking a second LLM. Training output remains private or a review candidate until the relevant publication checks pass.
